Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC data flow - follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap of asks we captured on the call:
   - PII scope: patient identifiers + clinical notes flagged as PHI by your team
   - Data residency: processing and storage must remain within US commercial regions
   - Logging/retention: you need access logs for 12 months and the ability to purge model inputs after 30 days
   - Egress controls: no outbound connections from the VPC to public endpoints; outbound only to whitelisted S3 buckets and internal telemetry endpoints

2) What I'm attaching: initial draft network/dataflow diagram and our Private (VPC) deployment whitepaper for your security team to review.

3) Proposed next steps:
   - Rachel (cc) to run through SOC 2 / evidence checklist and flag any gaps (ETA 2 business days)
   - Vivek to provide pricing guidance for a Private deployment with dedicated networking and retention options
   - Alex / Priya: confirm any additional regulatory constraints (e.g., state-level data residency) and share current architecture diagram if available

If that looks right I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week with our security engineer to walk the diagram and egress controls.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC data flow - follow-up & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming PII scope: includes MRN, full name, DOB, and free-text clinical notes. We'd like the option to redact PHI before sending to the model if needed.
- Data residency: must remain in US; we are fine with commercial regions (no gov cloud) as long as controls are in place.
- Retention: 30-day auto-purge of inputs is ideal, but we may need to retain logs/audit trail for 12 months as you noted.
- Egress: we cannot allow DNS-based egress or public internet calls from the inference hosts. Anything outbound must be to whitelisted endpoints under our control.

I attached our internal network diagram (sent separately to your team) and Priya will share the compliance questionnaire this afternoon.

Can we lock in the follow-up with your security engineer on Thursday 12/23 at 10:00 PST?

—Alex
Alex Gomez
VP of Engineering, AcmeHealth
alex.gomez@acmehealth.com

Alex —

Thanks for the detail. I'll start mapping the SOC 2 artifacts and list any missing evidence items. Initial ask: can you confirm the logging destination for audit logs (S3 bucket ARN or Splunk endpoint)? We typically provide both a logging-forwarder option and an on-host retention configuration.

I'll also include a short note on how our 30-day input purge interacts with trace logs (we keep second-order metadata for 12 months unless you request purging).

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC data flow - follow-up & next steps

Rachel / Marissa —

Attaching our compliance questionnaire and internal network diagram (sent to Marissa's team). For the logging destination: we can provision an S3 bucket in our acct (arn: arn:aws:s3:::acmehealth-logs) or provide a Splunk HTTP intake endpoint. We prefer S3 for long-term retention.

On the purge behaviour: we need guarantees that raw inputs (clinical notes) can be purged on demand within 24 hours of request; metadata/audit logs may be retained per policy.

We're on for the 12/23 security call — please share the calendar invite.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Compliance | AcmeHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC data flow - follow-up & next steps

Hi all —

Thanks for the responses and the questionnaire, Priya. Quick update after our internal sync: 

- Security call: sorry for the schedule noise — our security engineer is available on 12/30 at 10:00 PST (Rachel will lead). Will that work for you? If not, we can do 01/04.
- Egress controls: Redwood Private supports egress only to whitelisted endpoints inside your VPC via controlled NAT/egress gateways; we can block DNS-based outbound and only allow IP-level whitelisting to your S3 endpoints.
- Purge guarantees: we can implement on-demand raw-input purge within 24 hours and document the operational steps; audit metadata retention for 12 months is standard, and we can discuss shortened retention windows during contract.
- Next deliverables from us: updated network diagram with explicit egress gateway config, a sample runbook for on-demand purge, and SOC 2 artifact map (Rachel). Expect these by 01/04.

I've attached the updated diagram and the Private deployment dataflow PDF. If all good, Vivek will follow up on pricing/options for a Private deployment with dedicated capacity and the retention add-on.

Thanks —
Marissa
